FF6-EVENT-000487: the fresh, exhaustive re-audit the prior tick's own missing_behavior called for is now complete, and it found a genuine, previously-undocumented gap rather than merely confirming one's absence: `_check_limits` (from_bytes's own upfront gate) inspects only the ZIP central directory's own declared metadata, never the member's real compressed stream, and OraContainer.read() (called unconditionally by both load() and validate(), not only the opt-in resolve_asset() path) delegated fully to zipfile.ZipFile's own eager, unbounded .read(). Proven directly via tracemalloc against a member whose declared size and crc32 are forged to describe only a small prefix of a much larger real payload: the pre-fix code succeeds silently (no exception at all) while peak memory scales with the REAL payload's own size (2.06MB for a 10MB real payload, 323.5MB for a 150MB real payload), not the declared one. Fixed with `_bounded_read()`: decompresses through zipfile.ZipFile.open() in fixed 1MB chunks instead of the module's own unbounded `.read()`, raising OraLimitError once cumulative real output exceeds the container's own validated budget. After the fix, the identical attack measures a flat ~2.1MB peak regardless of whether the real payload is 10MB or 150MB -- independently reverified at both sizes and again from the installed, non-editable wheel. Every one of this obligation's own six named requirements now has direct, literal proof: large sparse archives (ORA-STREAM-COMBINED-BUDGET-PROOF), lazy-read instrumentation (spy point corrected to zipfile.ZipFile.open, the new place a member is actually touched), flat-memory checks (new, literal tracemalloc measurement, directly satisfying this obligation's own release_gate for the first time), cancellation (ORA-STREAM-BUDGETS-CANCELLATION-PROOF), and every resource limit including this newly discovered and closed gap. Audited every zipfile/ZipFile usage across the entire ora package: lifecycle.py's own usage is write-side only, no vulnerability there; _check_mimetype's own unmodified archive.read() call remains safe because it is gated by a prior STORED-compression-only check, where no declared-vs-real mismatch is structurally possible. DISCLOSED, non-blocking nuance: `_bounded_read()`'s own chunk_size (1MB) is a hardcoded implementation floor, not derived from ResourceLimits -- a caller configuring max_decompressed_bytes below 1MB would still see up to ~1MB transient peak memory per read() call before their own smaller budget is enforced. This does not violate the obligation's own rule_text (memory is bounded, just not to arbitrary sub-megabyte granularity), and DEFAULT_LIMITS.max_decompressed_bytes is 2GB, so this is a non-issue for realistic default usage.
